r.정치 구도: The constitution gives the president sweeping powers, and in practice power is concentrated in the president and his inner circle. A 2020 constitutional amendment effectively reset the count of presidential terms, opening the way to long rule. Elections are held, but serious opposition candidates are often barred from registering or jailed, and independent media and civic groups have been shut down under the 'foreign agent' law. United Russia, the majority party in parliament, backs government policy. Since the war in Ukraine began, even criticizing the war has become punishable.

t.why: A permanent member of the UN Security Council that, with the United States, holds most of the world's nuclear warheads. It has sold huge amounts of oil, gas, grain and fertilizer to the world. After annexing Crimea in 2014 and launching a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, it is under sanctions from the United States, the EU, Japan, South Korea and others, and it was removed from the G8 in 2014. As gas to Europe dwindled, world energy prices swung wildly; it now gets by selling crude to China and India. It has grown closer to China, North Korea and Iran and voices views different from the West's in BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
t.rel: It seeks to preserve its influence over former Soviet states: it is at war with Ukraine and fought Georgia in 2008. With Belarus it forms a Union State and has stationed troops and even nuclear weapons there. Since Finland and Sweden joined NATO, most of its western border now touches NATO, and it has grown closer to China and North Korea.
t.korea: Korea established relations with the Soviet Union in 1990. Before sanctions it was a big market for Korean cars and appliances, and several Korean companies had factories there, but many withdrew after the war began. Korea joined Western sanctions after the invasion of Ukraine. Now Russia's growing military cooperation with North Korea, including a mutual defense treaty, ties it directly to security on the Korean Peninsula. The Russian Far East has a history of Koryo-saram, and the Arctic shipping route and Siberian gas are areas of cooperation Korea has long been interested in.
t.know: Russia has 11 time zones: when it is morning at the eastern end, it is still the night before at the western end.
etext: Its reserves of crude oil, natural gas and coal are among the largest in the world, and it has big shares of wheat, fertilizer, aluminum, nickel, palladium and uranium enrichment. A large part of the state budget comes from oil and gas taxes.

After the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Europe sharply cut its imports of oil and gas, and much of its assets abroad were frozen. It sells crude at a discount to China and India and evades sanctions with a fleet of aging tankers.
Defense spending has soared, and arms factories and military-related jobs have driven growth. But labor is scarce and prices have risen, so the central bank has raised interest rates sharply.
